rules.title: Santa Ana Algorithmic Rent-Setting Software Ban
rules.requirement: Landlords and software providers would be prohibited from selling, licensing, providing, or using algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data (like real-time rents, lease renewals, and occupancy levels) to set rental prices for residential rental property in Santa Ana. Tenants could sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Ordinance (algorithmic rent-setting ban, pending final vote March 3, 2026; not yet codified)
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, approved on Tuesday, Feb. 17, for a first reading and set for a final vote on March 3, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the software relies solely on publicly available or aggregate historical data, or is used to comply with affordable housing program requirements

rules.conflict_note: Article indicates ordinance passed first reading Feb 17, 2026 with final vote scheduled March 3, 2026; status at time of article drafting is pending, not yet finally enacted.
